races.name: Ladbrokes 'Bet £5 Get £30 New Customer Offer' EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Ashina
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly trained by David O'Meara with Daniel Tudhope engaged — a reliable northern combination — returns from 65 days off with only one start behind her (sixth at Newmarket, Good), and will need a genuine pace to get into this from off the bridle.

runners_data.name: Dadawada
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves partners this prominent racer who finished fifth over 5f on Good ground last time; Christopher Kellett's yard is winless in four over the 14-day window, but Dadawada's forward-racing profile is naturally suited to tracking Oh So Slow Sloth and striking late.

runners_data.name: Desert Smoke
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's hold-up filly has two runs at 6f on Good, finishing sixth and fifth, giving her more experience than most rivals here; Paul Mulrennan takes over and she will need the race to be genuinely run to peel off the back and get involved.

runners_data.name: Fly Smartly
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar's prominently raced filly showed a placed effort over 5f on Good and steps up to 6f here; Donagh O'Connor rides and her willingness to race forward from the gate gives her a tactical advantage in what looks a compressed-pace contest.

runners_data.name: Lady Titania
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke sends out this prominent type fitted with a tongue-tie on her second start after finishing seventh at Newmarket; Sam James takes the ride and Burke's 14-day strike rate of 8/46 gives quiet confidence, though her Newmarket run was unimpressive.

runners_data.name: La Flor Granada
runners_data.note: Unraced Fahey debutante with Oisin Orr booked — that is a yard-jockey pairing that can win first time out — racing style is completely unknown, making scenario planning for her impossible beyond recognising the raw potential upside.

runners_data.name: Myesme
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's unraced newcomer with Jason Hart aboard; Bethell's yard has been showing respectable form (7/29 over 14 days) and Hart knows the yard, but with no public form, she is a pure unknown quantity on style and ability.

runners_data.name: Next Of Kin
runners_data.note: William Haggas's lightly raced filly showed a promising third on debut at 6f on Good — identical conditions to today — with Cieren Fallon, who retained the ride, booked again; a yard operating at 8/52 over the fortnight and a clearly relevant form line makes her a notable factor without being a confirmed pace shape.

runners_data.name: Oh So Slow Sloth
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies' filly is the sole confirmed front-runner and will lead from the gates; tagged with a style-fit flag noting she races somewhat out of role, and with a 85-day absence and a trainer winless in 11 recent runs, her chance of holding on depends entirely on whether the even gallop she sets is too slow to be pegged back.

races.paceDynamic: Oh So Slow Sloth is the lone confirmed pace-setter and will push forward from the gates to dictate on the front end, with Dadawada, Fly Smartly, and Lady Titania tracking prominently behind. With no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, Oh So Slow Sloth sets a controlled, sustainable gallop over Ayr's flat 6f on Good ground — a tempo that will not burn off the mid-to-back runners but will compress the race into a straight-line quickening contest from the two-furlong pole. Ashina and Desert Smoke, both confirmed hold-up operators, will need the pace to be genuine enough to reel in the leaders off a true-run race, which is not guaranteed with only one front runner. This race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent-to-lead horses who travel smoothly in the first half and quicken from the front, with hold-up runners reliant on the pace being stronger than it is likely to be given the lone front-runner scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Oh So Slow Sloth dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the prominent brigade cannot peg it back in the straight.
scenarios.body: Oh So Slow Sloth sets fractions it can sustain without pressure, and the fillies tracking in behind — Dadawada, Fly Smartly, Lady Titania — are best placed to challenge but may lack the decisive kick to collar a relaxed leader; Next Of Kin, with her promising third on debut at this trip and Good ground, could quicken to lead the challengers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the tracking prominent runners — Dadawada or Fly Smartly — travels smoothly throughout and produces the sharpest turn of foot off a steady tempo.
scenarios.body: With Oh So Slow Sloth controlling the pace, a horse sitting a length or two off the shoulder will inherit the best position to strike when the race ignites in the final furlong; Fly Smartly's placed effort over 5f on Good ground and Dadawada's consistent form suggest both are capable of delivering that challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the hold-up runners Ashina or Desert Smoke are able to find a clear run and produce a sustained late rattle.
scenarios.body: Ashina, trained by David O'Meara with Daniel Tudhope aboard — a potent combination in northern maidens — drops in from a 65-day break and might be sharper than her sole run suggests; Desert Smoke has two runs under her belt on this exact trip and going combination, giving her the clearest profile for a late swoop if the fractions suit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutante Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two unraced fillies, La Flor Granada or Myesme, is significantly ahead of expectation on debut and catches the field cold.
scenarios.body: Richard & Peter Fahey send La Flor Granada on debut with Oisin Orr booked, a combination that occasionally produces a ready-made juvenile winner, while Myesme's Edward Bethell yard has been in decent form; either would need raw talent to overcome inexperience, making this outcome the least probable but not impossible.

watchPoints.text: Oh So Slow Sloth's 85-day absence combined with a trainer in poor recent form (0/11 over 14 days) means fitness is a genuine question — if she ties up in the final furlong, the whole race shape collapses and prominent chasers inherit a different contest entirely.

Next Of Kin is the only runner with a form line that is an exact match for today's conditions (3rd, 6f, Good, debut) and Haggas/Fallon is a live combination — watch for her to be prominent at the two-furlong pole if the tempo is on her side.

La Flor Granada and Myesme are both unraced and their unknown styles could disrupt the expected pace map if either breaks fast and contests the lead with Oh So Slow Sloth, turning a one-runner pace scenario into a more pressured contest.

Fly Smartly steps up from 5f to 6f for the first time — if she settles better over the longer trip than she did sprinting, the extra furlong may unlock more of her form and see her finish strongly from a prominent position.

Lady Titania runs in a tongue-tie on her second start for the resurgent K.R. Burke yard; equipment changes at this stage of juvenile careers occasionally signal a significant step forward, and she is worth monitoring in the betting market movements before post time.

races.name: 'Ladbrokes Get More With Racing Bet Builder' Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Charcon
runners_data.note: Haslam-trained 3yo who wants to race further back than this pace map shows; stepping up to a mile here suits on paper, but all five career runs have come over shorter trips and his Good-ground record shows no wins or places in similar conditions — that combination of trip query and style compromise tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Hawksworth
runners_data.note: Quinn yard 3yo returning after 45 days off with a modest form string (7-5-11 in three runs); Good ground isn't a proven issue but this is a career-best trip and he naturally wants to come from well off the pace — a truly run race would help, which is not what this shape is delivering.

runners_data.name: Royal Baroness
runners_data.note: Smith-trained 3yo who has shown her best form over 8f on Good ground — a 3rd and 4th at that trip give her a live each-way angle; she's a natural off-the-pace type tucked into a crowded midfield, and the 66-day absence is worth noting given she runs fresh without obvious issue.

runners_data.name: Sanny Doo
runners_data.note: Goldie-trained 3yo who ran only two days ago at a longer trip on Good ground, posting modest figures across nine career starts; a true hold-up horse who will likely drift to the rear naturally regardless of the map position, and the quick turnaround is a physical flag given her uninspiring recent form.

runners_data.name: Hostelry
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old Ruth Carr mare who wears a visor and has been a model of consistency — five consecutive 5th-place finishes at 8-9f on Good ground tells the full story; she's a genuine hold-up type but actually holds a natural midfield-to-prominent position in this field, and the 9-day turnaround presents no concern.

runners_data.name: Millbuie
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and sole pace-setter in this race; Whillans-trained 5yo who wears a tongue-tie and blinkers, with a 10-day turnaround, and his recent 3rd over this course-and-distance distance gives him a concrete tactical advantage as the uncontested leader on Good turf.

runners_data.name: Ring Of Gold
runners_data.note: Easterby 9yo wearing a visor whose form string reads 5-4-7-7-7 and who hasn't troubled the scorer in the last 15 runs on Good ground; a natural hold-up horse who will race at the tail of the field in practice, and the short rest (9 days) follows a run where he finished seventh.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Nature
runners_data.note: Goldie 4yo last seen 14 days ago; placed on Good ground at 8f and showed a reasonable effort at 11f in softer conditions — trips suggest he's stretching back to a mile here, and his genuine hold-up style means he'll need the pace to be honest enough to close from behind, which is not guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Bridgefoot Rambler
runners_data.note: Hanlon Irish-trained 4yo wearing a hood; his 3rd at 8f on Good ground is his standout effort and he naturally prefers to be held up, meaning he's been pushed forward in the map display but will likely drift back in reality — the trainer has only one runner in the past 14 days (0 from 1) which provides limited confidence.

runners_data.name: Concert Boy
runners_data.note: Scott-trained 6yo who wears blinkers and hasn't won in 15 Good-ground starts; his best recent effort was a 4th over 8f on Standard, and he's a genuine hold-up type who needs a truly-run race to land his chance — this pace shape doesn't obviously serve him.

runners_data.name: Due Respect
runners_data.note: Rutherford 4yo wearing a visor who was only out six days ago; five consecutive Good-ground runs all over 6-7f suggest the step up to a mile is an experiment, and despite the map placing him in midfield he is a natural rear-tracker whose trip concern is the primary issue.

runners_data.name: Game Management
runners_data.note: Quinlan 5yo returning from a massive 314-day absence; his most recent hurdles form over 17f complicates the flat picture and while he won once on Good ground over 8f, that was some time ago — the layoff combined with the trip switch from long-distance obstacles makes him a significant unknown.

races.paceDynamic: Millbuie is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner Ayr mile and, critically, has no rival likely to seriously contest the lead — meaning he can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on Good turf. With no pace pressure, Millbuie will set his own fractions, and on a flat track that favours horses allowed to stride on rather than produce a sharp finishing burst, a steadily-run race is the most probable shape. The redistribution note is significant: Bridgefoot Rambler, Due Respect, Charcon, Sanny Doo, Ring Of Gold, Royal Baroness and Hawksworth are all genuine hold-up or off-the-pace types pushed into the midfield graphic because there are simply too many true hold-up horses for the map to accommodate at the rear — the majority will still race at the back end of the field. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently behind Millbuie or secure an early position just off the pace, as a steady gallop set by one uncontested front-runner will almost certainly not produce a late sprint that rewards deep closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Millbuie Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Millbuie bowls along in front without serious challenge and sets a measured, even pace throughout the mile.
scenarios.body: Millbuie dictates entirely on his own terms, and with no rival applying pressure the pace will be moderate enough that he retains reserves into the straight; horses who track him in the prominent berth — particularly Hostelry, who has deep Good-ground form at this trip — are ideally placed to pick him off.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Posse Fills Gaps
scenarios.trigger: If several of the redistributed midfield types push forward early and create a more genuinely competitive pace behind Millbuie.
scenarios.body: The pace thickens slightly as runners like Bridgefoot Rambler or Due Respect — whose natural instinct is to race nearer the pace — press forward from the off, meaning the race is run at a honest clip and the finish opens up for those with a touch of resolution.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If Millbuie sets a deceptively fast early clip that drags the field through the first half and leaves them vulnerable in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A fast-run mile on Good ground at Ayr can catch prominently-ridden horses flat-footed late, allowing genuine hold-up types who have been patient — Concert Boy or Spirit Of Nature — to reel in the leaders off a strong pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Upsets From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight, causing a scrappy finish where a horse finding clear air at the right moment pounces.
scenarios.body: In a moderate race at this class level, a runner like Royal Baroness or Hawksworth, tracking midfield and gifted a gap on the outside, could benefit from the chaos of 12 runners filling the straight.

watchPoints.text: Millbuie sets the entire tactical agenda here — if he bowls out in front unopposed and the field fails to apply any pressure before the home turn, he is dangerous to be left alone with a clear lead.

Bridgefoot Rambler and Due Respect are flagged as redistribution runners: watch the early stages to see if either pushes forward naturally — if so, the pace quickens and the race shape shifts materially from the dominant scenario.
Sanny Doo ran only two days ago; watch for any signs of freshness or residual fatigue in the parade ring and early running — quick turnarounds at this level on Good ground can catch horses flat.

Game Management has been off for 314 days and was last seen over hurdles at 17 furlongs — watch to see how he settles in the early stages, as a freshened-up runner with this profile can either be very forward or badly need the run.

Hostelry's consistent placing record (five 5th places) on Good ground at this trip makes her a useful pace barometer — if she gets a prominent pitch and still can't win, it tells you plenty about the quality ceiling of the entire field.

races.name: Ladbrokes 'Big Daily Boosts On Racing' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Keep Me Stable
runners_data.note: Second-time-out quickly after just three days, Linda Perratt's six-year-old has solid 7f good-ground form (placed twice in similar company) and will look to press Kelpie Grey from the off, making him one of the primary beneficiaries of a pace-controlled scenario.

runners_data.name: Carmel Valley
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's three-year-old holds genuine good-ground form at this trip, placed twice on similar conditions, and Jason Hart's positional intelligence could see her travel efficiently from off the pace — genuine each-way contender if the tempo is fair.

runners_data.name: Black Rock Beauty
runners_data.note: Fahey-trained three-year-old who won over 7f on good and carries strong course form; though her natural style is hold-up and she's squeezed into midfield by the size of the hold-up contingent, she's one of the few with the raw form to justify a market position if she can get clear air late.

runners_data.name: Albeyours
runners_data.note: Tudhope takes the ride on Hollinshead's five-year-old, whose best form is on soft or standard — the good ground here is a concern — and while normally a hold-up horse, she'll be racing a touch closer than ideal given the crowded rear of this field.

runners_data.name: Joshuas Dream
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old has a form string littered with double-figure finishes at 6f on similar ground, and the step to 7f for Billy Garritty is not an obvious fix; forced to race closer than preferred, the profile does not inspire.

runners_data.name: Novak
runners_data.note: Jardine's seven-year-old has placed four times recently without winning, consistently finishing in the mix at 7-8f, but his best form is on soft; racing out of his natural hold-up position on a flat good-ground track, the task is harder than his consistency suggests.

runners_data.name: Stoneywell
runners_data.note: Hollinshead runner wearing a hood who has been beaten 7th or worse in five consecutive starts, all at 7f or beyond on varying ground; 52 days off and no wins on the board make this a tough ask even if he finds his natural running position.

runners_data.name: Tropez Power
runners_data.note: Walford's veteran wears a visor and has a deeply unencouraging recent record — six starts without a top-five finish at 7-8f on good — and being asked to race closer than his natural style further limits his chance here.

runners_data.name: Yaaser
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's eight-year-old has run just two days ago, which warrants monitoring for freshness, and while he has placed at 7-8f on good ground twice recently, the weight of 135lbs and a winless run stretching back makes him an unlikely beneficiary even from a reshaped pace map.

runners_data.name: Catton Lady
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners Easterby's five-year-old, who is proven in second twice on good ground at 7-8f and arrives 38 days fresh; she stays further than most here and could be the one genuine hold-up horse who benefits if the pace quickens late enough.

runners_data.name: Gressington
runners_data.note: Scott's five-year-old wears blinkers and has been beaten 6th or worse in all six recent starts on good at 7-8f; consistent underperformance and no wins on this surface make this a very difficult betting proposition.

runners_data.name: Pal Joey
runners_data.note: Haslam's four-year-old wears a tongue-tie and has most recent form at 5-6f — this 7f trip on good appears beyond his comfort zone, and a record of 1W from 15 on good ground underlines the concern about the conditions.

runners_data.name: Kelpie Grey
runners_data.note: Goldie's six-year-old is the race's sole front-runner and sets the entire pace narrative; he has raced over 6f almost exclusively and the step to 7f is an unknown, though Mulrennan will look to exploit his uncontested lead and if the trip suits he becomes the race pivot.

races.paceDynamic: Kelpie Grey is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner 7f handicap and will look to dictate from the outset under Paul Mulrennan, setting what figures to be a controlled, sustainable gallop on good ground at Ayr. With only Keep Me Stable offering any genuine prominent cover, Kelpie Grey is unlikely to be pressured into a suicidal pace, meaning the tempo will be moderate rather than punishing. This field is packed with hold-up horses — Black Rock Beauty, Novak, Stoneywell, Tropez Power, Yaaser, Albeyours and Joshuas Dream are all genuine come-from-behind types who cannot all find their natural position and will be forced to race closer to the pace than ideal, further reducing the pressure on Kelpie Grey. The tactical verdict is clear: a single uncontested pace-setter on a flat track with a comfortable gallop strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and kick, or those with the class and efficiency to close from just off the pace — true deep closers are disadvantaged by the lack of early tempo to exploit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kelpie Grey Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Kelpie Grey is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable gallop and the field fails to produce a sustained mid-race challenge.
scenarios.body: Kelpie Grey sets a measured pace down the far side, builds momentum turning for home and holds on as the closers find the tempo too moderate to generate a winning sustained run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Keep Me Stable tracks Kelpie Grey closely and a modest pace sets up a front-two finish that the deep hold-up horses cannot bridge.
scenarios.body: Keep Me Stable sits a length or two off Kelpie Grey, gets a soft lead into the final 2f, and the redistribution of so many genuine hold-up horses into midfield means the closers can never generate enough momentum off a slow pace to peg back the front pair.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If a faster-than-expected pace develops or a runner in the prominent group goes too hard, creating a genuine collapse in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: An unexpectedly competitive gallop burns out the front-runners, opening the door for the one or two closers who manage to find their true position — primarily Black Rock Beauty (course-proven over 7f on good) or Catton Lady — to reel them in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate but a single mid-division horse picks a perfect line through the field and times a run to perfection.
scenarios.body: A horse like Carmel Valley or Novak, racing closer than their natural style but benefiting from good ground and Jason Hart's positional judgment, works through the pack to collar a tiring leader.

watchPoints.text: Kelpie Grey has never won beyond 6f — monitor whether Paul Mulrennan lets him stride clear freely or whether the extra furlong sees him empty in the final 100 yards, as the entire pace map hinges on his stamina.

The redistribution of seven genuine hold-up horses into midfield means the first 2f will be unusually congested in the middle of the pack — watch for scrimmaging, losing ground early, or jockeys being forced wide, which will cost ground on a flat track with no downhill assist.

Keep Me Stable runs for the second time in three days — freshness and recovery should be monitored in the paddock and at the start, as any dullness would remove the only genuine pressure on Kelpie Grey.

Black Rock Beauty's redistribution note masks the fact she has the strongest recent form in this field at the trip and surface — if she can find a clean run from midfield rather than being bottled up, she remains a live danger regardless of the pace shape.

Catton Lady is the only confirmed hold-up horse not flagged as redistributed, meaning she has the best chance of all the true closers of securing her natural position at the rear — watch whether she gets a clean run through a very congested field in the straight.

races.name: Ladbrokes 'Get More With Ladbucks' Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Northwest Passage
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's four-year-old takes the lead role by default here and Jason Hart will control fractions; won over 10f on good but has shown a tendency to fade late on longer trips, and the step back up to 12f after a 36-day break is a question mark — style-fit tag reflects this is not its optimal setup.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Acklam
runners_data.note: Two wins from seven runs on good ground is an encouraging record for Joanna Mason's mount, and the recent win over 13f suggests this trip is well within range; a natural hold-up type who was genuine at the track last time, the key is whether a modest pace gives enough of a test to bring stamina into play.

runners_data.name: Star Cast
runners_data.note: Jake Dickson's claim helps at the weights and the form string of 113211 is striking — three wins in last six including over 10f on good; races prominently and that suits perfectly in a race where the pace is likely to be set by a single front-runner, making this a strong positional fit.

runners_data.name: Regalian
runners_data.note: Consistent placed efforts in better company at shorter trips but the handicap history at 8f on standard and recent poor form figures of 63-688 do not inspire confidence stepping up to 12f; blinkers fitted, but the distance and lack of win at this trip on good are genuine concerns.

runners_data.name: Obito
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes over on a horse with 13 runs on similar going, showing two wins and seven placings — this horse is at home in these conditions; natural hold-up runner and the volume of closers in this field creates traffic risk, but Tudhope's tactical awareness at least offers a chance of finding the seam.

runners_data.name: Mano Chicago
runners_data.note: Andrew Mullen partners a horse who has placed at 10f on good multiple times but whose form reads more like a solid each-way type than a winner; blinkers on and 49-day break slightly elevate concern, though the trainer Iain Jardine has six runners in the last fortnight suggesting the stable is in form.

runners_data.name: Break The Bank
runners_data.note: David Allan rides a horse that has placed at 10f on good ground twice recently and the form is consistent, but a true rear-end closer pushed into midfield on the map due to the congestion of hold-up types — the style-fit discount is warranted, and a 16-day turnaround with blinkers again is workmanlike rather than eye-catching.

runners_data.name: Pearl Eye
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old has won twice and placed four times in 15 runs on similar going, making it arguably the most course-and-conditions reliable horse in the race; a natural hold-up runner placed in midfield on the map due to field congestion, and the 14-day turnaround is brisk — Mulrennan's experience is the key positive.

runners_data.name: Simply Ruby
runners_data.note: Dianne Sayer has no runners in the last two weeks and this four-year-old has yet to place on similar good ground in two attempts; mapped to midfield despite being a true hold-up type, and a trip up to 13f last time suggests stamina is there, but the form figures of 4137-6 do not build confidence at this level.

runners_data.name: Cisco Disco
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who won at 10f on heavy and has six good-ground runs returning only one win and one place; Sean Kirrane rides a horse that is prominent in style but whose recent form of 1-8706 is a sharp decline — unlikely to hold the lead against Northwest Passage at this level.

runners_data.name: Lorca's Waltz
runners_data.note: William Haggas and Cieren Fallon is an attractive combination for a three-year-old stepping up from 8f; a natural hold-up type carrying a style-fit discount for its midfield mapping, but 1W1P from four goes on similar ground and the Haggas yard is firing (8 from 52 in 14 days) — if the pace is slow this horse's sprint finish is the danger.

runners_data.name: Molinari
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old for Martin Todhunter with a 16-day break and a modest record of 0W1P from 15 similar-going runs; races prominently but the form string of 204-86 and limited ground from the trainer's 14-day record (0/4) make this a very tough case to construct.

runners_data.name: Boy Named Sioux
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's three-year-old is stepping up considerably from sprint distances — last five runs all at 6f-8f on standard or soft, so 12f on good is a significant and unproven demand; a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield due to redistribution, and the inexperience at this trip is the dominant concern.

runners_data.name: Ziata
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's three-year-old won over 10f on good last time and Kaiya Fraser keeps the ride — the progressive form string of 3-2531 with a recent win is the best momentum angle in the race; prominent racing style suits the predicted single-pace scenario and the 14-day turnaround after a win reads as a confident stable move.

races.paceDynamic: Northwest Passage is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead likely to press hard from the outside, Jason Hart can dictate a controlled, honest gallop over this 1m2f on good ground at Ayr. Star Cast, Cisco Disco, Molinari and Ziata will track up prominently but none carries the profile of a horse that will go to war with Northwest Passage for position in the early stages, meaning the pace is likely to be sustainable rather than punishing. The field is loaded with hold-up types — Lorca's Waltz, Pearl Eye, Break The Bank, Simply Ruby, Boy Named Sioux and Mano Chicago are all natural closers, but with so many needing to come from behind they cannot all find clear daylight through the same gap late on; those mapped to midfield due to redistribution will not be racing in their preferred position and should be discounted in pace-shapes that require them to close from the very back. A steady-to-honest single pace suits horses who can race prominently in touch with Northwest Passage and produce a sustained finishing effort from two furlongs out — prominent racers and hold-up horses with tactical speed to close in midfield are the favoured profiles, while true deep closers face a maximum-traffic scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Northwest Passage sets a fair, uncontested gallop and prominent trackers time their runs from two out.
scenarios.body: Northwest Passage bowls along in front at a sustainable clip, with Star Cast and Ziata sitting just off the pace in the perfect stalking position; the pace is honest enough to string the field out but not so fierce that the leader weakens dramatically, meaning the first two home come from the front third. Prominent types who have avoided traffic trouble hold a decisive positional advantage over closers caught wide or trapped in behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Slow Fractions, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Northwest Passage is allowed to bowl along at a crawl and the race turns into a dash from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A very modest pace collapses the field together and the winning move comes from a horse with raw turn-of-foot rather than stamina; Lorca's Waltz, trained by William Haggas and possessing a sharp sprint pedigree, is one of the few genuine hold-up types with the acceleration to capitalise despite being mapped out of natural position. Obito, with 13 runs on similar going and proven tactical speed, and Mano Chicago are also well-placed to fire from midfield if the gaps appear at the right moment.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threading Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to suit and one redistributed closer finds a clean passage at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A true end-to-end gallop set by Northwest Passage finally suits the deepest closers, and a hold-up type who has been patiently ridden finds the rail gap or swings wide to deliver a challenge; Spirit Of Acklam, who has won twice on similar going at 13f and 10f and drops back with a reliable pilot in Joanna Mason, is ideally suited if the race is truly run. Break The Bank's repeated placed efforts on good ground at 10f also give it a realistic chance if it can weave through, though its redistribution status and style-fit tag temper confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Northwest Passage is allowed a completely uncontested lead and the pace is pitched perfectly to deny closers the run-in they need.
scenarios.body: Ivan Furtado's horse has won from prominent positions before and with Jason Hart dictating every fraction on a flat track, if the gap to the closers is never bridged in the straight the leader simply gallops them into the ground. This scenario is the least probable because Northwest Passage's recent form shows a tendency to weaken late over longer trips and the sheer volume of midfield and prominent horses provides at least one danger with a genuine turn of foot.

watchPoints.text: Star Cast and Ziata both race prominently for trainer Gemma Tutty — watch whether Jake Dickson (5lb claim) and Kaiya Fraser slot in directly behind Northwest Passage early, as that position could be decisive if the gallop is honest.

Lorca's Waltz is a Haggas-Fallon combination with recent winning form, but is a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to redistribution — watch whether Fallon elects to drop it out fully or makes an early move to overcome the positional disadvantage.

Spirit Of Acklam with Joanna Mason is the most proven hold-up performer in the field on similar going (2W3P from 7 runs) — watch whether a genuinely strong pace develops to set up the late run, as without it this horse's stamina advantage is neutralised.

With six confirmed or probable hold-up types converging on the same patch of ground in the straight, watch for a significant traffic incident between the three- and one-furlong markers — horses drawn widest may be forced to go the long way round, gifting the rail-runners a clear advantage.

Northwest Passage's last three runs over 10f-12f on good or soft show a record of 2nd, 5th, 10th — watch whether Jason Hart elects to inject a burst of pace at halfway to blunt the closers rather than crawling to the straight, which could fundamentally change which scenario plays out.

races.name: Ladbrokes 'Insure Your Acca On Football' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Velvet Skies
runners_data.note: Redistributed to the lead despite a natural hold-up profile; on good ground she has a poor sim-going record (0W0P from 2 runs) and is racing out of her comfort zone tactically, so a style-fit discount applies even if she controls the tempo.

runners_data.name: Water Of Leith
runners_data.note: Consistent claimer for Jim Goldie on good ground (1P from 6 sim-going runs), ran just two days ago which raises freshness questions over 6f; holds up naturally and the sheer number of closers in this field makes a clean run through traffic uncertain.

runners_data.name: Henery Hawk
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt runner who has placed three times on good ground from four tries, showing he handles the surface reliably; a natural hold-up type and at 7 years old needs everything to fall right, but David Allan is an astute handler of these sprint handicaps at Ayr.

runners_data.name: Edmond Halley
runners_data.note: Young apprentice Cian Horgan takes the ride for Edward Bethell but this horse has shown no win or place on good going in three attempts and has missed the frame on softer surfaces too; the step back to 6f from recent 5f form is a concern and the going record offers little confidence.

runners_data.name: Head For Freedom
runners_data.note: Michael and David Easterby filly who has won once and placed twice on good ground from six runs, making her one of the more solid good-ground performers in this field; a 57-day break is the main query, but if sharp enough on return she has the profile to sit handy and stay on.

runners_data.name: Lord Abama
runners_data.note: Michael Dods runner who carries a hood and has the best sim-going strike rate for place finishes (1W3P from 10 runs), yet his true racing style is deep hold-up and the redistribution to midfield means he will likely be further back than that map position suggests — style-fit tempers his chance.

runners_data.name: Macedonian
runners_data.note: Wears a visor for Dods and has never won on good ground in six attempts; a genuine closer whose last five runs show he contested 7f events and now drops back to 6f — the shorter trip may sharpen him, but his inability to get his natural position in this cluttered field is the key tactical obstacle.

runners_data.name: White Umbrella
runners_data.note: Christopher Kellett's veteran wears a hood and is a pure hold-up type pushed into a midfield map slot; his good-ground record shows zero wins or places from three runs on the surface and the trainer's 14-day record (0/4) adds a negative angle.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 6-year-old wears a visor, ran just two days ago, but has an outstanding good-ground profile — 1W3P from 12 runs — and was the only horse in this field to have won over 6f on good ground recently; Paul Mulrennan is a significant positive booking and he may be one of the few hold-up types genuinely capable of finding his natural position from a forward draw.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Terms
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 3-year-old wears a hood and has contested 5f events at the main; moved up in trip to 6f today, which could suit on good ground, but his sim-going figures (0W0P from 4 runs) and youth in a 16-runner field leave questions; Andrew Mullen adds experience at least.

runners_data.name: Monastere
runners_data.note: Karl Thornton's Irish raider has won and placed on good ground before, but carries a finishing-fade flag which is a serious handicap in a race where the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to create a proper late-running opportunity; his redistribution to midfield from a true hold-up style compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: Sixcor
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's 8-year-old wears a cheekpiece and has a fine good-ground record — 1W4P from 10 runs — with a win over 5f; stepping up to 6f today and meeting a crowded midfield, but genuine speed over a shorter trip could translate well if a gap appears in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Ski Angel
runners_data.note: R Mike Smith's 6-year-old is partnered by 3lb claimer Amie Waugh and has placed once on good ground from 10 attempts; has shown proximity to the frame over 5f and 6f on good, but a 14-day break and low OR of 45 suggest she needs everything to fall right at big-field level.

runners_data.name: Red Walls
runners_data.note: Lisa Williamson's veteran has spent all recent form on standard-going (AW) where he has placed once; his good-ground record shows just one place from three runs and the switch back to turf after 34 days off with an unfamiliar 3lb claimer in Jack Nicholls creates multiple layers of uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Baby Rover
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's 4-year-old has strong good-ground credentials (1W3P from 9 runs) and shows recent 6f form with placings; Greg Fairley is a capable jockey who could position him forward from early on, making him one of the natural beneficiaries if a prominent berth can be secured in a pace-light race.

runners_data.name: Lanarra
runners_data.note: R Mike Smith's lightly-raced 3-year-old has placed twice on good ground without winning, with a consistent string of frame efforts at 6f; ran just two days ago like her stablemate Ski Angel, but the hat-trick of close finishes — 2nd, 3rd, 3rd, 4th — signals consistent competitiveness and William Pyle's low-key approach could see her sneak through late.

races.paceDynamic: Velvet Skies is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner 6f handicap and, despite being a natural hold-up horse redistributed to the lead, will likely be allowed to bowl along at a sustainable gallop given the near-total absence of genuine pace opposition. With no rivals likely to press her hard from the gates, the tempo should be honest but not fierce — a controlled, single-file race that progressively stretches the field in the final two furlongs. That setup hands the advantage squarely to horses who can sit just off the pace in the first three or four positions and sustain their effort through the dip and up to the line, rather than those attempting to close from deep. This field is saturated with hold-up types — Macedonian, Lord Abama, Pivotal Terms, Doon The Glen, Monastere and others all have genuine come-from-behind profiles but are mapped to midfield simply because the race has no room to accommodate them all at the back; the horses most likely to actually secure a forward position from the draw and early running are Doon The Glen, Pivotal Terms and Baby Rover, with the rest forced wider and deeper than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Pacer Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Velvet Skies dictates an uncontested, metronomic gallop and the field settles in a compact bunch behind.
scenarios.body: Velvet Skies sets every fraction from the front with zero pressure, and horses who can travel prominently in her slipstream emerge fresh enough to sprint past in the closing stages; the rail line from stalls 1-5 becomes prime real estate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If two or three horses manage to track Velvet Skies closely and produce a sustained challenge from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A slightly faster-than-expected pace allows those sitting second or third to time their run perfectly and overpower the leader inside the final furlong; horses that handle good ground and have shown a consistent knack for placing close up carry the biggest advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is genuinely brisk and the leaders tie up in the final 100 yards, creating a gap for hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: Horses dropped in midfield but with strong finishing ability begin to pick off tiring rivals from the two-furlong marker; however, this scenario is constrained by the volume of redistributed closers who will be forced wider than ideal, limiting its likelihood.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the absence of genuine pace creates an unusually slow early tempo and every group in the field arrives at the final furlong almost simultaneously.
scenarios.body: With all runners on the bridle longer than usual, jockeyship and draw become decisive and the result could emerge from almost any position; apprentice claim holders who can arrive late and unannounced are the hidden danger in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Doon The Glen ran just two days ago for Jim Goldie and Paul Mulrennan takes the ride — watch whether Goldie is running two horses (alongside Water Of Leith) with a specific tactical plan, as Doon The Glen's exceptional good-ground record makes him the most dangerous horse in the race if he gets a clean passage.

The sheer volume of redistributed hold-up horses (Lord Abama, Macedonian, Pivotal Terms, Doon The Glen, Monastere, Sixcor and others) means the midfield will be severely congested from the two-furlong pole — watch for traffic jams that could derail even the best-placed closer.

Velvet Skies is a natural hold-up type forced to lead and carries a STYLE_FIT discount of 0.80; if she fades badly in the final furlong after controlling the race, the entire pace scenario collapses and a late wave of horses could arrive simultaneously — creating chaos and a blanket finish.

Baby Rover and Lanarra both have credible good-ground form at 6f and run for smaller stables; watch their draw and early positioning — either could find a forward slot that the higher-profile redistributed closers cannot access in such a competitive, crowded field.

Head For Freedom returns from a 57-day absence for Michael & David Easterby who show 2/22 over 14 days — watch market moves late on, as this trainer can have horses ready first time back and her good-ground record (1W2P) is the strongest win-conversion figure among the leading hold-up types in this field.

runners_data.name: King Chaos
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type, 11 days since last run, trainer Rebecca Menzies winless in 11 runners over 14 days — all recent starts are on Standard, which makes today's Good turf an unknown surface switch; needs to settle and produce a late effort.|

runners_data.name: Penelope's Sister

races.paceDynamic: Positive Thoughts is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 1m2f handicap and, with no genuine pace rival looking to take her on from the front, she is set to control proceedings at a measured, sustainable tempo over Ayr's flat mile-and-two. The bulk of the field — Lesrico, King Chaos, Precious Spartan, Penelope's Sister and others — are genuine hold-up or midfield types who will be content to track her at a distance, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly pressured and the early fractions should be moderate. Several runners flagged as redistributed — Idyllic, Recobella, She's Got Bottle, Lightning Galaxy and Parole Officer — are true hold-up horses pushed into the midfield mapping because the rear of the field is over-subscribed; they are unlikely to be racing as far forward as their map position suggests. On a flat course at Good going with one uncontested leader setting a controlled tempo, this race shape most clearly favours prominent-to-midfield horses with a turn of foot who can sit just off the pace and quicken when Positive Thoughts kicks or ties: horses like Naturalia and Ravenscraig Castle who race prominently are best placed to exploit the predictable shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Positive Thoughts Dictates Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Positive Thoughts bowls along at a comfortable clip with no rival willing to close her down before the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Positive Thoughts sets a controlled pace from the front, the field string out behind in orderly fashion, and she either finds enough to hold on or the closest prominent trackers — Naturalia and Ravenscraig Castle — arrive late but find her tough to peg back; the lack of true pace pressure means the front-end position is a genuine asset.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Naturalia and Ravenscraig Castle sit just off the pace and produce the superior turn of foot in the straight.
scenarios.body: Both prominent racers have solid form at this trip on Good ground — Naturalia has four placed efforts at 10-12f and Ravenscraig Castle has shown stamina — and a moderate pace set by Positive Thoughts sets up a sprint from two furlongs out that suits those who've been travelling well throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely collapse-worthy or the field fans wide in the straight giving ground to genuine closers.
scenarios.body: Lesrico has tactical flexibility and King Chaos has course form, and either could benefit if Positive Thoughts ties up after making too much use of herself from a wide draw; however, because several apparent hold-up types are redistributed from their true position and will not be sitting as deep as ideal, the probability of a clean late swoop is diminished.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Positive Thoughts goes too fast early, the race becomes strung out and late closers scramble home in a messy finish.
scenarios.body: This low-probability shape requires Positive Thoughts to overcook the pace, which is unlikely given she is ridden by the experienced Jason Hart in a flat-going context; redistributed hold-up horses like Idyllic or Recobella would need to be racing in genuinely deep closing positions to benefit, but their style-fit scores indicate they are unlikely to find their natural rear berth.

watchPoints.text: Naturalia is drawn to sit prominently under Paul Mulrennan and her four recent runner-up finishes at this trip on Good-type ground make her the horse most likely to ambush Positive Thoughts in the straight — watch for her to be settled in second or third throughout.|

Positive Thoughts (Jason Hart) goes off unchallenged from the front, but she has never raced beyond 8f in her life — if the step to 10f finds her out in the closing stages, the race could open up for the prominent pair.|

She's Got Bottle is returning from 297 days off and, while she has ability, her redistribution out of her natural hold-up berth and the layoff together make her a significant each-way risk to followers — watch for signs of ring-rustiness in the paddock.|

Ravenscraig Castle's 10f good-ground placed form and the 7lb claim for Cara Tuke make him an each-way interest in Scenario A and B — if he travels smoothly into the straight in third or fourth, he could be closer than his OR of 57 suggests.|

Recobella's last run was a win over this trip on Good going, but her true hold-up style is compromised by where she will actually race today — watch whether Jack Nicholls (3) elects to push her forward earlier than ideal to compensate.|

runners_data.name: Tee Aitch Aye

runners_data.name: Rugby Union

runners_data.name: Onyeisi
runners_data.note: Karl Thornton's 3-year-old wears a hood (b) and Jason Hart takes the ride; five consecutive runs at 10-13f on good ground all without a win or place (0W0P, 5/15 sim-going) paint a consistent picture of a horse yet to find its level, and being a displaced hold-up type here adds another layer of complication.|

races.paceDynamic: West Tyrone is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, with no genuine rival to push him from the front, he is likely to control proceedings at a measured, sustainable gallop over this flat 1m2f trip on good ground. The pace will be honest but not frantic, meaning West Tyrone dictates tempo from the outset and the field fans out behind in a strung-out formation with the large hold-up contingent forced wide or deep to find daylight in the straight. On good ground at Ayr over this trip, a controlled single pace-setter typically sets up a race that rewards horses travelling prominently or just off the leader rather than those making up ground from the rear. This race shape firmly favours hold-up types who can sit close enough to the pace to land a telling blow — though this field holds considerably more genuine hold-up and prominent horses than the race map can accommodate at the rear, with Royal Blaze, Spirit Catcher, and Ceinture d'Orion the most likely to actually secure a position close enough to the pace to matter, while Sweet Kiss, Glasses Up, Motawaared, Tee Aitch Aye, Farabove The Limit, Rugby Union, and Onyeisi are all true hold-up types who will be competing for limited ground in the pack.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: West Tyrone Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If West Tyrone bowls along in front at a true but comfortable gallop and the field never applies sustained pressure, setting up a race decided by class and position from the turn.
scenarios.body: West Tyrone controls the tempo throughout, and horses closest to him — sitting second or third early — are best placed to pounce as the straighter Ayr home stretch unfolds with no late-finishing cavalry charge materialising.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up types who manage to slot just behind the leader early enough track West Tyrone into the straight and produce a decisive finish in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The tempo is steady enough that closers cannot generate the momentum to reel in those already travelling well, rewarding horses who have hidden cover but are not truly at the rear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply entering the straight and West Tyrone's controlled gallop collapses, causing the midfield to concertina and creating a gap for the deepest-positioned runners.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires true hold-up horses to get their natural position — which the crowded field largely denies them — so it is structurally less likely, but Royal Blaze's proven ability to finish strongly over 10f on good ground makes him a threat even from deep.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If West Tyrone is taken on early by one of the prominent-leaning horses not able to find their natural position, creating an uneven or falsely-run race that scrambles the field.
scenarios.body: A disjointed tempo could flatter a horse hitting the front opportunistically out of midfield, but the redistribution of so many genuine hold-up types into unnatural positions makes this scenario unpredictable and unlikely to reward true form runners.

watchPoints.text: West Tyrone's unchallenged lead could be the decisive factor — watch whether any of the redistributed midfield horses (particularly Tee Aitch Aye or Sweet Kiss) push forward early and compromise his controlled tempo, as any sustained pressure could fundamentally alter the race shape.

Royal Blaze is the in-form horse and Ewan Whillans has fired two winners from his last 13 runners over 14 days — watch how David Nolan positions him early, as getting into a tracking role behind West Tyrone rather than being trapped in the hold-up pack is the difference between winning and not.

The pack of seven genuine hold-up types forced into midfield creates significant traffic risk on the turn into Ayr's straight — watch for a wall of horses two furlongs out as Ceinture d'Orion and Spirit Catcher attempt to find gaps simultaneously.

Glasses Up's extraordinary good-ground record (12/15) at age 11 is worth noting — David Allan will attempt to get him cover early despite his natural instinct to race from the rear, and if he threads through cleanly his most recent win (13f/GOO, 21 days ago) confirms he retains ability.

Farabove The Limit's 187-day absence is the longest layoff in the field by a wide margin — watch her in the paddock and early in the race for any signs of ring rustiness that would confirm she needs the run.

runners_data.name: Vega Storm

runners_data.name: Our Randolph

runners_data.name: Wise Crack
runners_data.note: Went in over seven furlongs on good ground on latest start wearing a visor, which is the key form line; hold-up in nature but the visor sparked that win and Ruth Carr's 5/25 recent strike rate suggests the yard is in reasonable form — a potential place contender if the pace holds.

runners_data.name: Paroda Diva
runners_data.note: Dual winner over a mile (good-to-soft) and good ground for Patrick Neville; the 68-day break is a flag but the form at this trip and on this going is solid, and from a hold-up position she wants the pace to burn to give her a late run in the straight.

runners_data.name: Napolian
runners_data.note: Tudhope booked for David O'Meara's front-runner who won over a mile on good ground at OR below current mark; leads from the front and must cope with a direct challenge from Keep An Eye On It, but class and jockey edge give him the best chance of setting terms.

runners_data.name: Adiada
runners_data.note: Dods runner returning from a 293-day absence with limited form (no win in three career starts); the layoff makes its participation speculative and, while it holds-up naturally, there is little evidence it can produce a winning run fresh off such a long break.

runners_data.name: Keep An Eye On It
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Tony Coyle and Kaine Wood making a first start in four months; placed on good ground and has the speed to push Napolian hard for the lead, but the 120-day absence and 0-from-5 record over a mile raise doubts about its ability to sustain the effort to the line.

races.paceDynamic: Napolian and Keep An Eye On It are both confirmed front-runners and will fight for the lead from the off on this flat Ayr mile, creating a genuinely contested early pace rather than a soft, uncontested gallop. Tudhope aboard Napolian — the higher-rated of the two at OR 69 — gives that horse an edge in controlling the terms if he chooses to dictate rather than scrap, but Nolan on Keep An Eye On It has claims for the rail and will not yield cheaply. The resulting honest-to-strong pace over a flat, galloping track suits horses that can travel prominently with cover and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs rather than those required to make up significant ground. This race shape contains more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Vega Storm, Light The Night Up, and Hatamoto are true closers who will likely find themselves racing closer to midfield than their natural positions, reducing their effectiveness in a finish that could come sooner than they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Napolian and Keep An Eye On It fight for supremacy early and set a genuinely honest gallop that strings the field out.
scenarios.body: The strong early pace will drain the two leaders late, leaving prominent horses who settled just off the battle — such as Beckon or Our Randolph — with enough reserves to pounce from second or third in the straight. Ayr's flat, galloping mile rewards those who travel efficiently in the first half of the race and quicken at the two-furlong pole when the leaders begin to empty.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leaders Last Upsides
scenarios.trigger: If Keep An Eye On It or Napolian is able to secure a comfortable lead with minimal pressure and controls the tempo into the home straight.
scenarios.body: A horse allowed to stride on alone at a measured pace can quicken from the front and be very hard to reel in at Ayr over a flat mile with a fairly straight run-in. Napolian, who has won over course-equivalent ground, is the logical candidate to benefit if the pace shapes up in his favour with Keep An Eye On It backing off.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Dash Late
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early fractions are hot enough to collapse the leaders and a well-timed closer can sprint through.
scenarios.body: Hatamoto, in-form with two recent wins over eight furlongs and suited by good ground, has the form credentials to emerge late if the pace burns brightly, though being pushed forward from his natural hold-up position compromises his chance of finding clear running at the right moment. Paroda Diva also carries winning form over this trip on good ground and could fill this role if she settles quietly and is produced late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, True Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners neutralise each other entirely and the pace fizzles into the straight, allowing genuine hold-up horses to come from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because true hold-up horses (Vega Storm, Light The Night Up, Adiada) are already compressed into midfield and will not get the time or space late that they need; Adiada's 293-day absence adds further doubt about her readiness to produce a sustained finish. Light The Night Up, unbeaten in distance experience on good at this trip, is the best-credentialled of the closers but remains dependent on a race run to suit a profile she may not reach.

watchPoints.text: Napolian and Keep An Eye On It are on a collision course for the lead — watch the first two furlongs to see whether one blinks and drops back, because whichever horse secures the front cheaply becomes significantly more dangerous.

Hatamoto's hold-up style means David Allan will need to find a clear passage in the straight; in a ten-runner field with a compressed midfield, getting boxed in late is a genuine risk that could cost this in-form horse dearly.

Beckon returns from 117 days off — if the yard has not had a prep run before today, the fitness level is unknown and a prominent style in a strongly-run race will expose any lack of condition quickly in the final furlong.

Wise Crack wore a visor when winning last time for Shane Gray — confirm headgear is declared again today, as it appeared to make a material difference and removing it could significantly change this horse's profile.

Adiada's 293-day break means watch for a market move at the window — any significant support given Michael Dods' recent 4/29 strike rate would suggest stable confidence, but at face value this is a horse needing the run.
